directions.worker_1: Research short-horizon cross-sectional reversal and medium-horizon momentum in equity returns. Construct point-in-time signals from adjusted_close and open-to-open returns: 1-5 day reversal, 20-60 day momentum, and residual reversal after subtracting the cross-sectional median or equal-weight universe return. Test rank-based composite scores, winsorization, and simple regime conditioning using market breadth and cross-sectional dispersion. Build a complete generate_weights(history, universe) module that returns finite weights for every ticker, respects max absolute weight 0.02, gross <= 1.0, net within 0.01, and accounts for 5 bps transaction cost and 30 bps annual borrow via turnover control and edge thresholds. Report the hypothesis, exact signal timing to avoid lookahead, turnover estimates, train/validation behavior if you can simulate it, and known failure modes. Do not fit predictive models or mutate history in place.
directions.worker_2: Investigate risk, volatility, liquidity, and volume-based effects as an independent strategy family and as a filter for other signals. Using only supplied history, compute trailing volatility, downside volatility, average dollar volume, turnover, volume shocks, overnight/intraday gap behavior, and missing-data flags. Test low-volatility tilts, liquidity screens, volume-confirmation rules, and volatility-scaled position sizing under the 2% single-name cap. Evaluate whether high-turnover signals survive 5 bps costs and whether borrow costs matter for short legs. Deliver a self-contained generate_weights(history, universe) candidate that returns one finite weight per universe ticker, including zeros, with gross <= 1.0, net within 0.01, and no fitted predictive models. Explicitly describe ranking, neutralization, rebalance timing, and robustness to NaN/pre-listing rows.
directions.worker_3: Focus on portfolio construction and execution-aware weight design rather than discovering a new raw alpha. Take simple candidate scores such as medium-term momentum, short-term reversal, low volatility, and liquidity, and study robust ways to convert them into weights: rank composites, equal-weight top/bottom buckets, volatility scaling, correlation/diversification penalties, capped weights at 0.02, gross budget 1.0, and net exposure within 0.01. Design a turnover buffer that trades only when score changes exceed a threshold or expected edge exceeds transaction costs, and compare daily versus weekly rebalance logic using only past data. Produce a complete generate_weights(history, universe) module implementing your preferred constrained construction, with deterministic behavior and no model fitting. Include a critique of naive equal-weighting when the universe is small, because the 2% cap may force underinvestment; explain how your method handles that.
directions.worker_4: Act as robustness and validation lead. Explore alternative timing and data transformations that could improve or falsify the other workers' ideas: time-series momentum versus cross-sectional momentum, open-to-open versus close-to-close return horizons, skip-day effects, volatility-regime filters, market-breadth filters, and handling of NaN, pre-listing, and eligible flags. Design a lightweight train/validation diagnostic using only the supplied history: split by date, measure rank IC or long-short spread, turnover, drawdown, and sensitivity to lookback and holding period. Then propose and implement one conservative candidate strategy module generate_weights(history, universe) that blends only the most robust signals, returns finite weights for every ticker including zeros, and obeys max absolute weight 0.02, gross <= 1.0, net within 0.01, 5 bps transaction costs, and 30 bps annual borrow. Include a concise critique of overfitting risks and any assumptions that should be tested before deployment.
